chapter_title: The Chapter of the Three Seasons
chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by the oldest teaching layer. The substrate presents a systematic temporal-cosmological framework: three periods of cosmic history defined by the actions of cosmic agents (First Man, Living Spirit, Mother of Life, Ambassador, Sin). Both sides of every mapping stay within the cosmic system — no contemporary application, no institutional content, no exhortation. The only editorial material is dialogue frame attribution in paragraphs 1, 7, 8, 9, 10. The teaching about relative durations (first period longest, second shortest, third intermediate) is a distinctive substrate feature — systematic quantitative comparison of cosmic epochs. Jesus here is Jesus the Splendour, a cosmic emanation figure, not a historical reference. The chapter shows no editorial fatigue; it maintains substrate register throughout.

paragraphs.core_text: From the time when the light came forth and was crucified in the darkness, to the season when the Statue will ascend and the entire light, which was conjoined with the darkness, will be purified and cleansed. From that time on, from that time to the season of the end totals three seasons.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame formula: 'Once again the apostle speaks to his disciples:' and medial attribution 'He says:'
paragraphs.temporal_note: Frame formula wraps a substantive cosmological definition of the total timespan. The teaching content defines the three-seasons structure — the foundational framework for the entire chapter. 'Crucified' as a term for light's entrapment in darkness is distinctive Manichaean cosmological vocabulary.

paragraphs.core_text: Three seasons: from the time when the First Man went down to the abyss, and waged the war and the struggle against the King of the realms of Darkness and his other powers. He was victorious, while his sons remain behind with them in the worlds [... ...] in the [...] until he shall catch all of them [...] he bound them all up, so that not one of them escaped his hand. He won a great victory [... ...] The First Man spent human lifetimes and generations in the land of darkness, until he prevailed [...] ⟨p.56⟩ he fulfilled the will of the greatness that was commanded of him.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure cosmological narrative of the first period. The enumeration marker 'Three seasons:' launches the systematic teaching. All agents are cosmic (First Man, King of the realms of Darkness). 'Human lifetimes and generations' measures cosmic duration, not human history. The institutional score (2.73) likely triggered by 'generations' but this is cosmological time-measurement, not community reference.

paragraphs.core_text: Then they sent the Living Spirit, the Father of Life. He brought the First Man up from the struggle, he brought him up to the land of light. This is the first period, from the descent of the First Man to his ascent.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure substrate. The summary formula 'This is the first period, from the descent of the First Man to his ascent' is the teaching voice defining the temporal structure. Both sides of the mapping are cosmic: Living Spirit → rescue → land of light.

paragraphs.core_text: The second season is from the time when the First Man ascended. The Living Spirit came, and the Mother of Life. They set in order the things of the universe, they set up [...] the Father of Life and the Mother of the living set in order [...] the universe, up to the moment when they go out [...] it was reckoned to the second season.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure substrate defining the second period. Enumeration marker 'The second season is' structures the teaching. Cosmic agents (Living Spirit, Mother of Life, Father of Life) perform cosmic construction. Lacunae damage but no editorial content visible in what survives.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] the universe [...] the Third Ambassador spread [...] that is in the [...] living; he [...] he separated beauty from all the powers and scooped it up to the heights, he swept the waste to the abyss, and he [... ...] Now, from the moment when the Ambassador revealed his image he purified the light. Sin spurted up towards him. He hid his image. Sin came [...] from the darkness. It sculpted the trees and the abortions fell down. Afterwards they sculpted Adam and Eve in the flesh. Until the moment when Jesus was sent and he [...] as he performed there his will. He gave the hope to Adam, and ascended to the heights.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmological narrative of the third period. The Ambassador's image-revelation, Sin's reaction (personified cosmic agent), the sculpting of trees/abortions, and the creation of Adam and Eve — all cosmic process within the system. 'Jesus' here is Jesus the Splendour, a cosmic emanation figure who awakens Adam — not a historical reference. Both sides of every mapping remain within the cosmic architecture. The verbs 'separated', 'scooped up', 'swept', 'sculpted' describe cosmic manufacturing processes.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, from the time when the Ambassador displayed his image until the season when the Statue will ascend at the end, shall be reckoned to the third season.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summary definition of the third period, parallel to paragraph 3's summary of the first period. The 'Now' here is not an editorial bridge connective — it introduces a definitional statement that closes the three-period enumeration. Pure cosmic temporal mapping.

Heavily damaged. The surviving clear text is frame formula ('Then the disciples asked the apostle'). The fragments 'with each other in the light earth' contain the cosmological term 'light earth' but are too damaged to yield intelligible teaching. The question likely asked about the relative durations of the three periods, setting up the teaching in paragraphs 8-12.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] lasts long in the time that the First Man spent in the world of Darkness. It is a very great count of time, more than the (other) two seasons!
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame attribution: 'The apostle says to them'
paragraphs.temporal_note: Frame wraps a substantive teaching about the first period's duration exceeding the other two. The comparative temporal analysis is core substrate — systematic quantification of cosmic epochs.

paragraphs.core_text: The first season, which the First Man spent in the world of Darkness, is how much longer than the time that this universe has been? While it is established?
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame attribution: 'His disciples say to him:'
paragraphs.temporal_note: Substantive cosmological question within the Persian pedagogical tradition. The question defines the next teaching unit: the ratio of the first period to the universe's duration. This reveals the teaching structure — it IS the substrate. The question stays entirely within the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: If you should say that [... ...] it is small, if you should [... ...] to him [...] and you consult [...] you will tell him: Twenty times! It is greater again in this other one that you will consult: Thirty times! Less also is this other one [... ...] people will receive the {} of the trees [... ...] the years and the generations [...] earth to the heights. This is [...]
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame attribution: '[He replies to them]:'
paragraphs.temporal_note: Heavily damaged but the surviving fragments show quantitative comparison of cosmic durations ('Twenty times!', 'Thirty times!'). The second-person address ('if you should say') is pedagogical voice within the teaching tradition, not editorial application — both sides of the inquiry remain within the cosmic system. The numbers suggest a systematic ratio teaching that was the core point of this passage.

paragraphs.core_text: This is the third period, from the time when the Ambassador revealed his image until the Statue will ascend from the lump. It again, that time, is greater than the intermediate; but it does not come equal to the time of the First Man. For this intermediate season, in which the Father of Life and the Mother of Life constructed the universe with its orders, is shorter than that of the First Man.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure substrate. Systematic comparison of the three periods' durations: first > third > second. This is the core teaching point — a quantitative ordering of cosmic epochs. All agents and domains are cosmic. 'The Statue will ascend from the lump' uses a distinctive cosmological image for the final gathering of light.

paragraphs.core_text: Great is the period of the First Man! It lasts longer than the season in which the Ambassador displayed his image, until the dissolution of the world and the Statue ascends. From the time too when the Ambassador displayed his image, until the dissolution of the universe [... ...] when the Father of Life and the Mother of Life shaped the universe.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Recapitulation of the duration hierarchy. The exclamatory opening 'Great is the period of the First Man!' is teaching voice — emphatic statement of the systematic finding, not devotional exhortation. All content remains within the cosmic temporal system. 'Dissolution of the world/universe' is cosmological eschatology, not contemporary application.

paragraphs.core_text: These are the [...] three periods of time that occur. ⟨p.58⟩
paragraphs.temporal_note: Closing summary of the three-periods teaching. The seam flag for 'These are the' is a false positive — this is not a bridge to institutional content but a natural closure to the enumeration. No institutional, exhortatory, or editorial content follows. The formula summarizes the cosmic teaching and closes the chapter.
